title: Assessing the potential mechanism behind the increase in miR-155-5p expression induced by Nsun2 inhibition during arsenite-triggered epithelial-mesenchymal transition in HaCaT cells
content:
Abstract
Arsenic exposure poses a significant global public health concern. Skin lesions serve as the primary diagnostic and grading criteria for arsenic poisoning in current diagnostic protocols, yet the underlying pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. In this study, we initially determined that both short-term exposure to high concentrations of arsenic and long-term exposure to low concentrations of arsenic can inhibit the expression of Nsun2 while promoting the expression of miR-155-5p, leading to the induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) -like phenotype in HaCaT cells. Subsequently, we employed cell transfection techniques to manipulate Nsun2 expression levels in HaCaT cells, demonstrating that Nsun2 knockdown exacerbates NaAsO2-induced EMT-like phenotype by upregulating miR-155-5p expression, while Nsun2 overexpression suppresses miR-155-5p expression, thereby alleviating NaAsO2-induced EMT-like phenotype. Furthermore, rescue experiments revealed that miR-155-5p knockdown partially reverses the EMT-like phenotype and associated cellular damage induced by Nsun2 downregulation. These findings suggest that sodium arsenite induces EMT-like phenotype in HaCaT cells by downregulating Nsun2 and upregulating miR-155-5p, thereby providing a potential mechanistic link to arsenic-induced skin damage.
